hypothesis: The bind-choreography parity audit's actionable correctness gap (D1, record 20261001-174500, bench 4e0f00d): all three rust exit cleanups - supervisor.rs run()'s tail (:487), worker.rs exit_after_close (:813), supervisor_lost.rs exit_orphaned (:129) - passed a cleanup-time socket_identity(path) read as their own 'expected' guard, comparing a fresh read with itself, so the guard never discriminated: any file REPLACED at the path after the bind was unlinked by the dying owner's exit. TS captures the identity at LISTEN time (daemon-supervisor.ts:879, daemon-mode.ts:718) and compares THAT at exit (daemon-mode.ts:1078-1080), so a replaced socket file survives the old owner. THE REACHABLE FAILURES: (worker, most reachable) a force-stopped D-state survivor wakes after the supervisor relaunches its replacement on the SAME deterministic worker-socket path (supervision.rs reuses descriptor.socket_path) - the survivor's late exit_orphaned/exit_after_close unlinks the replacement's LIVE socket, routes fail, the session bounces through the failure loop until the next relaunch cycle; (supervisor) an external sweep (tmpfiles age rules; the TS module names macOS dirhelper's 3-day $TMPDIR sweep) removes the socket file under a serving supervisor, a successor binds while the original serves its nameless listener - the original's exit unlinks the successor's LIVE socket and every new connect fails ENOENT while the socket looks alive.
approach: THE D1 FIX (TS-convergent 1:1, frozen surfaces untouched): bound_socket_identity captured immediately after bind_transport and before restrict_socket_path (the exact TS listen-callback order: capture -> ownsSocketPath -> restrict) at both rust bind sites - supervisor.rs run() and worker/connection.rs serve() - stored on Supervisor and Worker (std::sync::Mutex<Option<SocketIdentity>>, None until bind; named pipes keep None: no file to stat), and the STORED value passed at all three exit-cleanup call sites. cleanup_socket_path itself is unchanged (already a faithful port of TS cleanupDaemonSocketPath); no wire/TUI/prompt/behavior bytes change - the guard is daemon-internal ownership bookkeeping. FAILING-FIRST FIXTURES (permanent, the window_serves pattern): tests/socket_identity_guard_e2e.rs - three served-path oracles against the real binary (orphan_exit_never_unlinks_a_replacement_bound_on_the_worker_path via exit_orphaned; routed_shutdown_never_unlinks_a_replacement_bound_on_the_worker_path via the routed shutdown arm/exit_after_close; a_drained_supervisor_never_unlinks_a_replaced_socket_file via the supervisor's SIGTERM drain/run() tail) plus the missing still-ours control (routed_shutdown_removes_the_workers_own_socket_file; the other two still-ours directions are pinned by the in-tree controls worker_orphan_exit_e2e::orphaned_worker_exits_when_the_supervisor_socket_never_answers and supervisor_e2e::shutdown::a_sigterm_exits_the_supervisor_through_the_graceful_drain). Every oracle binds the replacement with the original file renamed aside first - the original inode stays allocated, so the replacement's dev+ino provably differs and the oracle can never pass vacuously on inode reuse (the trap socket.rs's own tests document: a freed inode can be handed straight back to a fresh bind) - and each carries a served-path precondition (the old owner still alive when the replacement binds; a clean exit-0 through the exit path under test), so a pass proves the cleanup actually refused the differing identity.
